summary.text: Maxwell's demon is a thought experiment, proposed by James Clerk Maxwell in 1867, that seems to break the second law of thermodynamics.
A tiny gatekeeper guards a door between two gas chambers, letting fast molecules pass one way and slow ones the other, so one side warms and the other cools.
Most scientists argue no device can really do this, and the puzzle stimulated work linking thermodynamics and information theory.

facts.label: Proposed by
facts.value: James Clerk Maxwell, in a letter of 1867

facts.label: Apparent effect
facts.value: Lowers entropy with no work applied

facts.label: Real experiments
facts.value: None shown to violate the second law

items.prompt: In the thought experiment, why does one chamber warm up while the other cools down?

options.label: The demon's body gives off heat
Fast molecules collect on one side and slow ones on the other
More molecules are pushed into one chamber
The door insulates one chamber better

items.explain: The temperature of a gas depends on the speeds of its molecules, so sorting fast ones to one side heats it and cools the other.

items.prompt: A demon opens the door only for fast molecules heading from A to B, and never lets any back. What would end up higher on side B?

options.label: Temperature and pressure
Only the speed of the door
Nothing; the sides stay equal
Temperature but lower pressure

items.explain: One-way passage of fast molecules raises both temperature and pressure on side B; passing molecules both ways gives only a temperature difference.

items.prompt: Why would the demon's trick be such a problem for physics?

options.label: It would make entropy fall with no work being done
It would show molecules do not move
It would make gases impossible to cool
It would prove entropy always rises faster

items.explain: The second law says entropy in an isolated system never decreases, yet the demon seems to lower it without applying any work.

items.prompt: An engineer hears that one chamber is hot and the other cold, with no energy spent. Why would that interest her?

options.label: A heat engine between them could extract useful work
It would let her destroy heat completely
It would cool both chambers to zero
It would make the gas weigh less

items.explain: A heat engine operating between the two chambers could extract useful work from the temperature difference.

items.prompt: A lab builds a gadget that sorts molecules a little like the demon. What do researchers say about such experiments?

options.label: They prove the second law is false
They match the thought experiment exactly
They differ from it and none violate the second law
They show the gadget needs no energy

items.explain: Experiments implementing forms of the demon all differ from the thought experiment and none has been shown to violate the second law.

items.prompt: Two metal blocks at different temperatures touch and are sealed off from everything else. What does the second law predict, the very thing the demon would undo?

options.label: The hot one gets hotter and the cold one colder
They settle at about the same temperature
The cold block sends heat into the hot one
Neither changes temperature

items.explain: By statistical probability the two bodies evolve to equilibrium with approximately the same temperature; the demon would reverse that.
